issue.title: Active-user data attribution for recordings/edits
issue.body:
### Current state on main

- Active user is tracked in KV: `src/services/storage.ts` — `getActiveUserId()` (`:101`), `setActiveUserId()` (`:105`), `switchActiveUser()` (`:153`), plus `getKnownUserIds()`.
- `recordings` table (`src/db/schema.ts:80`) has **no user column** — it links to a verse via `bible_text_id` only.
- The upload worker (#100) relies on the **server deriving identity from the Bearer token**, so the network path is attributed by token — but **local** rows carry no record of who created them, which matters for multi-account devices and offline review.
- `parseUserId()` (`src/utils/parseUserId.ts`) resolves the active user id for queries.

### Problems / why

- On a shared/multi-account device, two users can record against the same verse; without local attribution the app cannot show "your takes vs. theirs" or correctly scope My Work recording state.
- Upload attribution currently depends solely on whichever token is active at upload time; a recording captured by user A but uploaded while user B is active could be misattributed if the token isn't pinned per-recording.

### Target design

- Add a nullable `recorded_by_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id)` column to `recordings` via the #110 migration framework (coordinate with #99/#103 to avoid duplicate migrations).
- On capture (#97/#98 `addRecordingTake`), set `recorded_by_user_id = getActiveUserId()`.
- On upload (#100), upload under the **token of the recording's owner** when available (so attribution is stable regardless of the currently active account), or document that the active token is acceptable if product confirms single-user-at-a-time.
- Scope recording aggregates/My Work by the active user where appropriate (consistent with #104).

### Implementation steps

1. Add migration for `recordings.recorded_by_user_id` (via #110; bundle with the #99/#103 migration set).
2. Set the column on capture in `addRecordingTake` (#98) using `getActiveUserId()`.
3. In `recordingSync` (#100), resolve the owner's token via `getCredentials(recordedByUserId)` when present; fall back per product decision.
4. Update `Recording` DB types (`src/types/db/types.ts`).
5. Document the attribution policy (capture-time owner vs. upload-time active user).
6. Tests: capture sets owner; aggregates scope by active user; upload uses the owner token.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `recordings.recorded_by_user_id` exists (via #110 migration; not a duplicate migration).
- [ ] New recordings are attributed to the active user at capture time.
- [ ] Upload attribution policy implemented and documented (owner token preferred).
- [ ] Tests cover capture attribution and upload token selection.

### Test plan / verification

```bash
npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --ci
```

- Tests default `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:9999` via `jest.env.cjs`; **no live API required** — local SQLite/mocked DB.
- Do **not** use `FLUENT_USER_EMAIL`.

### Out of scope

- Account switcher UI (#84–#87), upload worker mechanics (#100), schema FK restoration (#99/#103).

### Links

- Epic: #118
- Related: #98 (capture), #100 (upload), #99/#103 (migrations), #104 (My Work scoping)

PR body already includes `Closes #105`, but the base is `mrace/feature/103-harden-user-projects-fk` (not `main`), so GitHub does not show a linked/closing issue in the PR sidebar until the stack (#246 → #248) merges and this PR is retargeted to `main`.

Closing as completed (tracker cleanup after repo audit).

**Evidence on `main`:** landed via squash merge of PR #248 (`a27ca5f`), which included the #105 / PR #251 work (`recorded_by_user_id` on `recordings`, capture attribution, owner-token upload path).
